analysis: The code flow: first checks if responseType is null. If null, it attempts to use legacyResponseType; if that is also null, it logs an error via event.error(Errors.INVALID_REQUEST) and throws ErrorPageException. If legacyResponseType is non-null, responseType is set to that value. Then event.detail(Details.RESPONSE_TYPE, responseType) is called. Afterwards, it checks if responseType equals 'CODE'. If not, it logs an error via event.error(Errors.INVALID_REQUEST) and throws ErrorPageException. The only runtime exceptions thrown are the explicit ErrorPageException instances. Since ErrorPageException is treated as a runtime exception (it is not caught or declared, implying it is unchecked), the method intentionally lets these exceptions propagate to a higher-level handler. There are no other statements (like null pointer accesses or array bounds) that would raise unhandled runtime exceptions. Therefore, no additional try-catch handling is required within this snippet.
